note: The machine-readable side of the style maps (style-maps.md): the axes a style is described on, the limits review uses for each of its checks with where each comes from, and the map entries a project's `style` may name. An entry's checks override the defaults for the checks on the axes it governs. 'ours' marks a number this project set itself (on its early agent pieces), not a number from a source; per the project's rule a limit is never set on agent pieces again, only from the literature or measured on professional work. A family's or entry's `published_mix` is the published long-term spectrum measurement `analyze` sets the master beside (Pestana et al. 2013's slope over 100 Hz-10 kHz); an entry's replaces its family's, and `borrowed` or `why_none` says why one is lent or absent. An entry's `tempo_bpm` is the tempo range its source gives (its map's tempo cell); `review` asks about a piece whose main tempo lies outside it, a half- or double-time reading counting as inside.

vertical.what: minor seconds and ninths between a sustained note and another part's note

outside_chord.source: Open Music Theory, Embellishing Tones (the kinds); Longuet-Higgins and Lee 1984 (strong positions); Temperley 2007 (rock melodies leave them unresolved)
outside_chord.what: notes on strong positions outside the written chord, not resolved by step

parallels.source: Open Music Theory, First-Species Counterpoint (the rule, for independent voices); the window and the doubled share are ours
parallels.what: parallel fifths and octaves between lines moving the same way

low_intervals.what: close intervals under their low limit

static_texture.what: every part repeating the same block of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars note for note; with processes_vary, only the runs of the span in which no filter sweep, gain automation or controller curve moves the sound

repetition.what: a part repeating a 1-, 2- or 4-bar cycle unchanged

literal_returns.what: a section repeating an earlier one note for note in every part

arrivals_thinner.what: an arrival section thinner than the one before it in notes per bar, parts or velocity

sections_alike.what: neighbouring sections with the same parts and nearly the same density and dynamics

stiffness.what: chord parts struck and released as one block

pushes.source: Tan, Lustig and Temperley 2019 (rock and pop melodies anticipate strong beats); Witek et al. 2014 (moderate syncopation)
pushes.what: no melody or accompaniment attack anticipating a downbeat or half-bar

restatement.source: Summach 2011 (pop sections state and restate an idea); Caplin 1998 (the sentence); the 8 bars are ours
restatement.what: a section whose melody bars restate no earlier bar's rhythm and shape

melody_durations.what: a melody of few duration values

melody_velocities.what: a melody of nearly flat velocity

transposed_samples.what: notes playing a sample transposed far from its root

highpass.what: a part's high-pass taking from the fundamental of its lowest note

widespread_lowpass.source: Senior 2012 (Sound On Sound, Q&A): widespread low-pass filtering seldom helps a mix and easily dulls it; the 12 kHz (the lower edge of air in the mixing books listed by Moffat, De Man and Reiss 2022), the half and the three parts are ours
widespread_lowpass.what: most parts other than the bass low-passed at or under 12 kHz

tempo_range.source: the tempo ranges the entries' sources give (their maps' tempo cells, `tempo_bpm`); reading half and double time as inside is ours
tempo_range.what: the piece's main tempo outside the range its style entry's source gives
